convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iMA indicators with simple EMA crossover entry/exit rules, fixed lot sizing, and standard MQL5 Trade library includes that are structural (CTrade, CPositionInfo, CSymbolInfo) not logic-bearing. No custom indicators, no grid/martingale, no multi-timeframe logic.

derived_values.name: ExtTakeProfit
derived_values.used_by: Buy/Sell order TP, trailing TP preserve

other_exits: Trailing stop activates when already in position and trailing distance + step exceeded; signal reversal closes opposite side before entering new trade

custom_logic_notes: Crossover detection uses bar [1] vs bar [0] (previous completed bar vs current forming bar). On crossover reversal, the EA first closes the opposite-side positions, then if flat (count_buys==0 && count_sells==0) it enters the new direction on the same bar. Trailing stop activation threshold is ExtTrailingStop+ExtTrailingStep (55 pips profit for buy, 55 pips for sell) before modifying SL; SL is then set to ExtTrailingStop distance (50 pips) from current price. The filling type auto-detects FOK→IOC→RETURN. No stop loss is set on entry orders (SL=0.0).
python_conversion_notes: EMA crossover logic is straightforward. Note that the MQL5 code uses MODE_SMA (not EMA despite the filename) — the indicator name 'EMA' is misleading; actual method is SMA. Digit adjustment (multiply by 10 for 3/5 digit brokers) must be replicated in Python. Trailing stop uses combined threshold (stop+step) for activation then sets SL at trailing_stop distance from price — this two-level logic must be preserved exactly. Entry gate requires both buy and sell counts to be zero (fully flat), not just no same-side position. The filling type detection chain (FOK→IOC→RETURN) can be simplified in Python backtesting to assume FOK or market order.
